source_name: EU TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) Search API v3
authentication: none observed for the search endpoint (POST https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search answered anonymously); the developer portal documents API keys for higher service levels, which were NOT used
free_tier: free, anonymous search queries answered without registration
rate_limits: UNKNOWN - no published numeric limit found; 9-request probe at 1.0 s interval was never throttled
licence: EU open data; TED notices are published by the Publications Office of the EU. Reuse terms were not verified in detail, so redistribution is recorded as PARTIAL.
update_frequency: daily (TED publishes notices each working day; not measured in this probe)
historical_coverage: notices from 2016 observed in probe results; total index counts in the millions (cn-standard 2,952,676 / can-standard 2,855,759 at probe time)
entity_identifiers: OCID is NOT returned by the search API
winner-name / winner-partname fields exist in the schema but came back null
timestamp_fields: deadline-date-lot / deadline-date-receipt-tenders (present in the field list)
contract-duration-start-date / contract-duration-end-date (present in the field list)
known_limitations: The awarded supplier is NOT exposed by the search API: winner-name, winner-partname, winner-country and winner-selection-status all return null even for a 2024 medical-device award notice (can-standard). A structured award->supplier link therefore cannot be built from the search endpoint alone.

Because full text includes the winner, an FT~"Medtronic" query returns 8,122 notices since 2024 - those are keyword hits, not awards to Medtronic. Reporting them as the firm's awards would be a category error.

The notice XML/PDF (which does contain the winner) lives on ted.europa.eu, which answers this client with a JavaScript 'Human Verification' challenge (HTTP 405). No anonymous bulk XML package was verified, and the challenge was deliberately not bypassed. bulk_download_available is therefore UNKNOWN, not YES.
CPV codes are procurement categories (e.g. 33100000 medical equipments). They are not device identifiers and cannot be joined to UDI/510(k).

Expert-query syntax is field-typed: `FT~"phrase"` for free text but an equality/in-list operator for enumerated fields; `~` on notice-type or classification-cpv returns HTTP 400. Any connector must encode this or it will silently mis-query.
publication-date in an expert query must be written YYYYMMDD, not ISO.
ted.europa.eu web pages (including /en/bulk-downloads) are not machine-readable for this client; the API is the only verified path.
research_value: Provides EU-wide public demand signal at notice level with a hard separation between contract notices (cn-standard) and contract award notices (can-standard), which is exactly the notice-vs-award layering MedRadar needs. Buyer names and CPV categories are available, so EU public buying of medical equipment can be counted by category and by purchasing body - but not by supplier, which must come from a different source.
cost_notes: free; no key used, no registration performed
